Among the oxidative stress responsive transcription factors, NRF2 aroused extensive concern for its important role in cancer.
For breast cancer, though, the sub-classification of breast cancer was also classified according to ER-positive and negative [17], the lack of ductal carcinoma, adenocarcinoma such morphological classification of discussion, and this degree of malignancy for breast cancer and NRF2 correlation also has important reference value.
On the one hand, NRF2 degraded intracellular carcinogens by activating downstream genes to prevent carcinogenesis [12]. On the other hand, chemotherapy drugs increased activation of NRF2, which can counteract the role of drug molecules and promote the cell survival, finally result in chemotherapy resistance. Immunohistochemical researches in non-small cell lung cancer [13] and epithelial ovarian cancer [14] demonstrated that high expression of NRF2 is relevant to platinum resistant.
